summary.text: Brian Fitzpatrick is the Republican incumbent, a former FBI special agent and federal prosecutor first elected to Congress in 2016 to succeed his brother Michael Fitzpatrick. He serves on the Ways and Means Committee and the House Intelligence Committee, where he chairs a subcommittee, and co-chairs the bipartisan Problem Solvers Caucus.

paragraphs.text: According to his official biography, Fitzpatrick was born and raised in Levittown, in Pennsylvania's 1st Congressional District, and graduated from Bishop Egan High School.

He earned a bachelor's degree from Penn State University and a law degree from the Dickinson School of Law, and his official biography says he holds a JD and MBA from Penn State through a joint degree program.

Fitzpatrick spent 15 years as an FBI special agent and federal prosecutor, including work as a supervisory special agent and special assistant United States attorney. His official biography says he was embedded with U.S. Special Forces during Operation Iraqi Freedom and served as national supervisor in the FBI's Public Corruption Unit.

That biography lists FBI honors including the FBI Director's Award and Investigator of the Year for his role as lead case agent in Operation City Lights, a public-corruption investigation in New York City. He is also a licensed attorney, certified public accountant and certified emergency medical technician.

Fitzpatrick won the 2016 general election for Pennsylvania's 8th Congressional District with 54.4% of the vote over Democratic state Rep. Steve Santarsiero, succeeding his older brother Michael G. Fitzpatrick, who did not seek re-election. The district is now numbered the 1st.

In the 119th Congress (2025-2026) he serves on the Ways and Means Committee, including its Health and Oversight and Investigations subcommittees, and on the House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence, where his official page lists him as a subcommittee chairman.

He co-chairs the bipartisan Problem Solvers Caucus and, according to his official biography, co-chairs nearly 20 caucuses and task forces and has been designated by House leadership as a Congressional Representative to NATO. He advanced unopposed from the May 19, 2026 Republican primary, receiving 44,365 votes.
